hook: Interviewer: This table has 1,000 rows... but COUNT(email) returns 847.
reels.hint: Pay attention to what COUNT counts....
reels.caption: SQL Puzzle #1: the table has 1,000 rows, so why 847? Comment your answer 👇 #sql #sqlinterview #dataengineering
reels.answer: COUNT(email) skips NULLs, so 153 customers have no email. COUNT(*) counts every row.

hook: Interviewer: This count skips rows that aren't active...
reels.caption: SQL Puzzle #2: why does != skip rows? Comment your answer 👇 #sql #dataanalyst
reels.answer: Rows where status is NULL disappear: NULL != 'active' is unknown, not true. Fix: WHERE status != 'active' OR status IS NULL.

hook: Interviewer: My LEFT JOIN lost the customers with no orders...
reels.code:
SELECT c.name, o.order_id
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o
  ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE o.status
    = 'shipped';
reels.caption: SQL Puzzle #3: my LEFT JOIN lost rows. Why? Comment your answer 👇 #sql #sqlinterview
reels.answer: Customers with no orders have a NULL status, so WHERE removes them and the LEFT JOIN acts like an inner join. Fix: move the filter into ON.

hook: Interviewer: 500 orders went in. 1,200 rows came out...
reels.code:
SELECT o.order_id,
       p.promo_code
FROM orders o
JOIN promotions p
  ON p.customer_id
   = o.customer_id;
reels.hint: Pay attention to the join key....
reels.caption: SQL Puzzle #4: 500 orders in, 1,200 rows out. Why? 👇 #sql #dataengineering
reels.answer: Customers with several promotions match several rows, so their orders are duplicated (join fan-out). Fix: join to one row per customer.

hook: Interviewer: AVG says 80. The real average is 64...
reels.hint: Pay attention to the last score....
reels.caption: SQL Puzzle #6: AVG says 80, the real average is 64. Why? 👇 #sql #dataanalyst
reels.answer: AVG ignores NULLs, so it averages 4 scores. If NULL means a missed test worth 0, the real average is 320 / 5 = 64. Fix: AVG(COALESCE(score, 0)).

reels.code:
SELECT version
FROM releases
ORDER BY version;
-- 1, 10, 11, 2, 9
reels.hint: Pay attention to the column type....
reels.caption: SQL Puzzle #7: why does 10 sort before 9? 👇 #sql #dataengineering
reels.answer: The column is text, which sorts character by character. Fix: ORDER BY CAST(version AS INT).
